scenes.vo: It doesn't. McDonald's is one of the biggest real estate companies on the planet.
In nineteen sixty one, its CFO, Harry Sonneborn, told Ray Kroc that burger margins were too thin. So they bought land instead.
Franchisees pay McDonald's rent, on top of royalties. About ninety five percent of restaurants are franchised.
So the franchisee flips the burgers, and McDonald's is their landlord.
Rent alone brings in roughly ten billion dollars a year, and it arrives whether or not you buy a Big Mac.
The burger is just the reason you walk through the door. The land is the business.
